prerequisites: Fundamentals of elasticity theory and structural mechanics
Successful completion of courses 'Mechanics 1' and 'Mechanics 2' are minimum requirements
Completion of modules 'Mechanics 3' and 'Numerical Methods in Engineering Sciences' is also highly recommended
Knowledge from the course 'Advanced Strength of Materials' would be beneficial

learning_outcomes.text: Apply classical approximation methods to elastic structural problems.
Justify the choice between beam, plate, and 2D continuum models for a specific problem.
Assess the quality and suitability of finite element meshes for 2D and 3D structural analyses.
Analyze numerical problems such as locking, hourglassing, or insufficient approximation order.
Perform static strength verification of components by analyzing the stress state, including stress concentration.
Numerically model simple contact and pressure problems.
Perform simple simulations in ABAQUS and compare them with analytical results.
Assess simulation results regarding accuracy and physical plausibility.
Independently analyze technical problems and select appropriate solutions.
Critically question simulation results and make reasoned decisions for further analysis steps.
Independently use digital tools for simulation and efficiently organize the work process.

syllabus_topics: Finite differences for partial differential equations: Prandtl's stress function in torsion problems; bending of elastic plates; longitudinal and bending vibrations of a rod.

FEM in 1D: Longitudinal strain of a rod, statics and vibrations. Linear and quadratic approaches; degrees of freedom of nodes, elements and the entire model; consistent nodal loads; element stiffness matrix and global stiffness matrix; local coordinates and Gaussian integration, convergence behavior. Comparison with Ritz's method with a global approach.
Beam bending: Bernoulli-Euler and Timoshenko (shear flexible). Locking, reduced integration, hourglassing, spurious vibration modes.
2D elements: Triangles, quadrilaterals, linear and quadratic approaches; isoparametric concept, Jacobi matrix. Assembly of global stiffness matrix. Stress evaluation and stress analysis.
Mesh generation and mesh quality. Imported meshes.
Stress concentration: Kirsch's problem. Mesh refinement.
Simple contact modeling. Hertzian pressure in 2D and 3D.
Fundamentals of modal analysis and model order reduction.
Large deformations of beams. Transient dynamics and time integration.
Introduction to ABAQUS: Handling the software package. Graphical user interface, individual modules. Preparation of the simulation, start of the analysis, post-processing.
Simple example problems in ABAQUS. Illustration of theoretical findings.
